title: The World of AI: Legal Models catalogue on Hugging Face
answer: The World of AI publishes a Legal Models page that catalogues the 1000 most-downloaded open legal models on the Hugging Face Hub, with licence, downloads, and release date, refreshed daily. Its most useful point is that it gives a dated, source-linked index of open models tuned for legal text, drawn from the Hugging Face Hub public API and sorted by all-time downloads. It is a reference page rather than an analysis, and it also points to the site's broader database of AI laws, lawsuits, and terms.

sections.body: The World of AI publishes this page as part of its AI ecosystem section, under technology and core infrastructure. It is a catalogue page titled Legal Models. The text says it covers the 1000 most-downloaded open legal models on the Hugging Face Hub, with licence, downloads, and release date, refreshed daily. It states that the data comes from the Hugging Face Hub public API, sorted by all-time downloads, and that every model links to its own Hub page. The page carries a last verified date of 2026-09-28. It also includes site navigation and promotional notes about books and services by Stephen R. Jordan and SRJ Consulting & Services.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page says it tracks the 1000 most-downloaded open legal models on the Hugging Face Hub. For each model it lists licence, downloads, and release date, and it refreshes this list daily. The models are described as tuned for legal text. The source of the catalogue is the Hugging Face Hub public API, sorted by all-time downloads, and every model links to its own Hub page. The page also describes the wider site as a searchable database built from the same source, covering state AI laws, a lawsuit tracker, a glossary, a tools directory, AI companies, a research library, an MCP server registry, compliance frameworks, sources, people, calculators, and weekly digests. It calls the site an atlas of artificial intelligence, covering what the law says, who is suing whom, and what the words mean. It says every page is rebuilt daily from primary sources and carries the date it was last verified. It states the site is free to read, free to cite, and free to query. The page also notes books by Stephen R. Jordan, including The Operating Discipline for AI Library series, available on Amazon, and a novel by SRJ Consulting & Services called The AI Lawyer, out 17 August 2026. It lists several audit and assessment service names.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The source states that the catalogue covers the 1000 most-downloaded open legal models on the Hugging Face Hub. It says the list is refreshed daily and sorted by all-time downloads. It gives a last verified date of 2026-09-28. It says the data source is the Hugging Face Hub public API and that every model links to its own Hub page. It states that the site is free to read, free to cite, and free to query. It says every page is rebuilt daily from primary sources and carries the date it was last verified. It gives 17 August 2026 as the publication date for the novel The AI Lawyer. It gives no model performance benchmarks, accuracy figures, or legal compliance metrics.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in Legal can use this page as a dated index of open legal models. It points to the 1000 most-downloaded open legal models on the Hugging Face Hub and records licence, downloads, and release date, which can help track which open models are available and how widely they are downloaded. Because every model links to its own Hub page, the page can act as a starting point for finding legal text models. The wider site also claims to track state AI laws, lawsuits, and terms, which may help a reader connect model availability to the legal landscape. The page itself does not evaluate legal accuracy, bias, or compliance, so it is a discovery tool rather than an assessment.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Legal

sections.body: This is a landing page with little substantive analysis. It does not provide model evaluations, benchmarks, accuracy figures, or legal advice. It covers only open models on the Hugging Face Hub, sorted by all-time downloads, so it is partial to that platform and that popularity measure. It does not cover closed or proprietary legal models. The page is dated by its last verified date of 2026-09-28 and says it is refreshed daily, but the harvested text is a snapshot. It is partly commercial, promoting books by Stephen R. Jordan and services and fiction from SRJ Consulting & Services. It also includes site navigation and service names, which are not explained in the text.
